Standard: For stores with the potential to re-contact the air vehicle post-safe separation (e.g., deployed systems such as first stage rocket boosters or inlet covers, loitering munitions, air launched effects and powered stores with loft trajectories), the store includes design features, system lockouts and limitations, or processes to avoid store-to-store and store-to-air vehicle contact. For systems without collision avoidance mechanisms, procedures exist to prevent contact post-separation (e.g., air vehicle deconfliction maneuver). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine store post-launch control systems to identify timing of post-launch events and potential sources of post-separation collision during intended stores operations. Analysis.
  (1) Perform analysis of the store fly-out model to identify limitations or procedures necessary to avoid store-to-store or store-to-air vehicle collisions, including errant engagements.
  (2) Perform FMECA of store systems to determine if failure modes increase likelihood of post-separation collision with other stores or the host air vehicle. Demonstration.
    (1) Evaluate the store OFP and flight control features using lab demonstration to verify that post-launch store features preventing store-to-store or store-to-air vehicle collision function as intended. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Perform and measure system properties (e.g., ejection forces, aero loads) to characterize mechanics related to store separation and post-separation events (e.g., staging mechanisms, deployed systems). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
      (2) Demonstrate the air vehicle can perform maneuvers to avoid potential debris, errant loitering munitions, or other post-separation recontact. Test.
    (2) Flight test: Perform with instrumented vehicles to characterize mechanics related to store separation and characterize fly out model (e.g. Time Space and Position Information data) of post-separation events (e.g., staging mechanisms, deployed systems) to ensure store-to-store and store-to-air vehicle collision does not occur IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 290.
    (3) Flight test: Perform to measure the actual separation distances and timing of events to show systems meet minimum store-to-store and store-to-air vehicle miss distances for all post-separation phases of flight. Validate predicted miss distances with measured flight test data to substantiate the full flight envelope for all release conditions and mixed load configurations.
